solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I start working beside railway, showing skill

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged, so I START is shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job next to the railway line and proves good at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns I START into ARTIST; 'showing' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: creative skill or craftsmanship is exactly what this noun names.

clue.text: Icy cold aboard lorry

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vehicle is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ARTIC is British slang for an articulated lorry (a large truck)
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A chill felt while riding in a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is the British name for an articulated lorry, a semi-trailer truck; 'aboard' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: polar regions are frozen, so the adjective means extremely chilly.

clue.text: They're required when arranging meetings by many

parts.note: in multiplication, three by four is three times four
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: Many people need these when setting up appointments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the multiplication sense, as in a room measuring ten by twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: to book appointments you must fix slots in a diary or schedule.

clue.text: Still kept up in second clamour? It'll do for sleep

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other combined pair

parts.note: a hue is an outcry, as in 'hue and cry'

indicators.note: in a down answer, kept up means written bottom to top

parts.note: still in the sense of yet, as in 'not yet done'

explanation.surface: A noisy moment that keeps on going; perhaps a nap will do the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept up' reverses the word for Still and 'in' places it in the second-plus-clamour pair; 'hue' is the outcry of 'hue and cry'. 'It'll do for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a spell of closing the eyes and dozing is slumber.

clue.text: Broken pieces I dropped in streams

indicators.note: something dropped in goes inside a container, here the word for streams

parts.note: streams runs, as water runs or flows

explanation.surface: Shattered fragments that I let fall into brooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: remains of something destroyed or wrecked are its broken pieces.

clue.text: Right to swap parts by proxy

indicators.note: the two halves of the word change places, front three letters to the back

parts.note: proper means right or correct

explanation.surface: Seems to be about the right to delegate roles to someone acting for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swap parts' splits PROPER into PRO and PER and exchanges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase used when signing letters on another's behalf, i.e. as their agent.

clue.text: Still asleep? It'll give you balance

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even more' or 'still more'
someone out cold or out like a light is asleep

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone is still dozing, and whether that restores equilibrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It'll give you' only links to the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb synonym: to level or equalise things is to bring them into equilibrium.

clue.text: Historic city favoured by deity

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: An ancient town enjoying a god's special favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the rock-cut Nabataean site in Jordan is a famous ancient town.

clue.text: Start theatrical run with actors describing various digs?

parts.note: a show opens when its run begins
the cast is the group of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A play's premiere with its cast, wondering about lodgings ('digs').
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like British slang for lodgings, natural for touring actors; here it means excavations.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for surface mining, where the pit is dug in the open air rather than underground.

clue.text: Contralto and soprano interweaving with — yes — rhythm band

indicators.note: threads interweaving are mixed through one another, so the letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for contralto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: Singers' voices blend with an affirmative beat in a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the abbreviation C is used for 'Contralto', while 'soprano' is used in full; together with YES and RHYTHM they make all seventeen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large ensemble of instrumental players is a kind of musical group.

clue.text: Local building in broadcast of my concert minuet

indicators.note: seeds broadcast are scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio transmission of my concert piece, played in a nearby hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the anagram signal; 'in' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a hall serving a neighbourhood for gatherings and activities is a local facility.

clue.text: Last features conforming with Society

parts.note: in step means conforming or in line with others

explanation.surface: The final aspects of something conform to the rules of a Society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' is not 'final': it is a shoemaker's last, a foot-shaped block, which has these arched parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Part relation: a cobbler's foot-shaped block includes the arched upper middle of the foot.

clue.text: Expert correctly recorded about one being commonplace

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, so it contains it

parts.note: sic is printed after a quotation to show it was copied exactly as written
A means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: A specialist's accurate notes about a single thing turn out to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC goes 'about' A to give SAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking imagination or flair, ordinary and dull.

clue.text: Trade sadly coming in low, not very lively?

indicators.note: one piece enters the other and sits inside it

parts.note: to low is to moo, like cattle

indicators.note: sadly signals that things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Business is poor and spirits are down: things are sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' scrambles Trade and 'coming in' places it within the cow's call; 'low' means moo here, not depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate pace, so not especially fast.

clue.text: Three articles about rising fashionable European city-dweller

indicators.note: the articles go around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the indefinite articles A and AN and the definite article THE

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means written upward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Grammar words on a trend that is gaining ground, describing a Continental townsperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the word for fashionable upward, and 'about' puts the three articles round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonym: someone from the Greek capital is a European urban resident.

clue.text: Pawns also leap squares initially

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A chess move: pawns too can jump squares at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess a pawn may advance two squares on its first move, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: people used by others for their own ends are manipulated instruments.

clue.text: See 9
Wrong about time, though unaffected by time?

indicators.note: the first word goes around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: immoral means wrong in an ethical sense

explanation.surface: A mistake concerning time, though apparently timeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside IMMORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: living for ever, never ageing or dying, so beyond the reach of passing years.

clue.text: Notes a lot of soft stuff and a lot of frozen stuff

indicators.note: a lot of but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: mush is soft pulpy matter

indicators.note: again a lot of but not all, so the end letter goes

parts.note: ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Jottings about plenty of soft material and plenty of frozen material.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSH loses its H and ICE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective sense: a sequence of musical tones or sounds makes up melody.

clue.text: Monster with insufficient excuse put in prison

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: insufficient means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse

explanation.surface: A beast with a weak excuse is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: ALIBI loses its last I and is 'put in' CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the misshapen savage slave in Shakespeare's The Tempest is a famous brute.

clue.text: Farm feature possesses point, while retaining unknown quantity

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: has means possesses
in algebra, x, y and z stand for unknowns
a tack is a small sharp-pointed nail

explanation.surface: Something on a farm has a point while holding an unknown amount, like the needle in the proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' puts Y inside HAS; 'while' is a link. The surface nods to looking for a needle in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large pile of stored dried grass is a common sight in a farmyard.

clue.text: Last of it's heaped and carried by wagon

indicators.note: take the final letter of the word

parts.note: rucked means gathered or piled up in a ruck, a heap

explanation.surface: The last of the load is piled up and hauled away by cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: moved goods by lorry or cart, conveyed by road vehicle.

clue.text: Long term cut for river

parts.note: to long for is to itch for

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an end or term is a limit or close

explanation.surface: A long term is shortened to suit a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb, to yearn. END loses its D. This river runs through Hampshire in southern England, past Winchester and Southampton.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chalk stream in southern England is a waterway.

clue.text: Bird identified from owl's wings in gold and brown

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other pair

parts.note: tan is a light brown
the wings of the word owl are its outer letters, O and L

explanation.surface: A bird recognised by an owl's wing feathers coloured gold and brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is the heraldic term for gold; 'in' places the owl's outer letters within the colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small European bunting, once eaten as a delicacy, is a songbird.

clue.text: Mock fan turning up without a ticket at the outset

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece encloses the other
in a down answer, turning up means written bottom to top

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in 'a football nut'

indicators.note: at the outset means take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Jeering at a supporter showing up without a ticket at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives TUN, which goes 'without' (around) A, then add the T of ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to jeer or ridicule someone is to provoke them with insults.

clue.text: Most vulgar of Parisian to puncture pie topping

indicators.note: something that punctures goes through and sits inside, so one piece is placed within

parts.note: the crust is the pastry on top of a pie
de is French for of

explanation.surface: The rudest of Parisians stabs a pie's pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Parisian' means the French word for 'of', which 'to puncture' drives into the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: coarsest, most offensive or rude.

clue.text: Endless chill one caught, giving stomach trouble

indicators.note: giving here closes the string of pieces, saying they combine to yield the result
endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: a chill is a cold
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone catches a lingering chill and ends up with a tummy upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: severe abdominal pain, often in babies, is a digestive complaint.

clue.text: Mistakenly thinks the album should include college drawing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another, holding it inside
mistakenly signals the letters are put down wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly believes a record should feature a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistakenly' rearranges THINKS THE ALBUM and 'should include' adds C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a quick small sketch or outline is a type of picture.

clue.text: Part of service showed no discrimination between candles?

definitions.meaning: a series of prayers with responses said in church worship
split into two words it describes setting fire to whichever wick came to hand

explanation.surface: Church worship, with someone lighting every candle indiscriminately.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into a verb and a determiner: kindled whichever one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long responsive prayer is one portion of a church rite.

clue.text: Pollutant found in a Guernsey sewer?

parts.note: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI
a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some contaminant lurks in a sewer on a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France; CI is their abbreviation. 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: precipitation made acidic by industrial emissions is environmental contamination.
